content:
I have been struggling with https://adam.math.hhu.de/#/g/alexkontorovich/realanalysisgame/world/Lecture3/level/2 for 5 hours today, even with the help of gemini pro.
This is the state of my game so far
Active Goal
 1 / ↑n < ε

Objects:
a: ℕ → ℝ
ε: ℝ
N: ℕ
n: ℕ

Assumptions:
ha: ∀ (n : ℕ), a n = 1 / ↑n
hε: ε > 0
hN: 1 / ε < ↑N
hn: n ≥ N
hn_real: ↑N ≤ ↑n
h1: 1 < ε * ↑n
h2: 0 < 1 / ε

I tried to introduce a new hypothesis like so
have h3 : (0 : ℝ) < ↑N := by bound

or
have h3 : (0 : ℝ) < ↑N := by linarith[h2, hN]

But both failed. Gemini pro's explanation seems incorrect. How should I understand why they fail?

Not to spoil all the solution, I have such working lines (my hi corresponds to your h2) 

have hi : 1 / ε > 0 := by bound [εpos]
have hNpos : N > (0: ℝ) := by linarith [hi, hN]

It was very helpful for me to work in Editor mode </>.
It is convenient to copy/paste, comment/uncomment multiple lines of code.
Indentions work (helpful for multiline proofs in lemmas).
Probably, the most relevant to your question:
Sometimes Lean Game Server shows a new lemma in the list of accepted objects, but Lean, actually, does not accept the proof marking (underlining) something wrong by red in the Editor mode. So, in the Editor mode, you can check what is really accepted on your previous steps of proof.
